newsitem.title: UK: Gold coin hoard on sale from treasure ship.
newsitem.headline: Gold coin hoard on sale from treasure ship.

text.p: A hoard of gold coins salvaged from the wreck of a British steamer went on sale on Wednesday with auctioneers confident the haul could make at least 1.5 million pounds.

After a two-year search in the Bay of Biscay, salvage expert Nigel Pickford found the remains of the Douro after a remote undersea camera spotted one of its crested porcelain dinner plates embedded in the sand.
Iona Sale, spokeswoman for the coin dealers Spinks, said the two-day sale had started with spirited telephone bids from collectors in Europe, South America and Australia.
"Interest was intense. We expect our final estimate of 1.5 million pounds will be exceeded," she told Reuters.
The Douro sank with the loss of 17 lives in 1882 when it collided with the Spanish steamer Yrurac Bat.
The ship, bringing wealthy passengers back on a voyage from South America, had 28,000 gold sovereigns in its safe.
The coins, dating from the reign of Queen Victoria, were minted in London, Melbourne and Sydney. The haul also includes a small number of Brazilian coins.
